limitations: Source-derived candidate; no local efficacy validation.
Original typed source inventory is not normalized; retain source identities and limits in the procedure/readsets.

applicability.scope: Diagnose TorchNPU device-HBM reuse, stream lifetimes, fragmentation and graph/private-pool retention before proposing allocator changes.
applicability.input_contract: Allocation failure/size sequence, device and allocator path, installed versions/settings, stream and graph-pool timeline, retained tensor references and allocator statistics with synchronization boundaries.
applicability.produced_artifact: A suspected allocator state transition with source evidence IDs, one eligible action, resource cost, counter-signals and a correctness-first verification/rollback plan.
applicability.refusal_point: Missing evidence supports only a conditional proposal, not a diagnosed leak; stop when external/custom/shared allocation ownership is untraced and keep baseline settings for unsupported versions or live-tensor capacity pressure.

recommendations: Separate stream lifetime protection from producer/consumer ordering, and distinguish live tensors, pending events, inactive splits and private-pool retention before tuning.
Match split or expandable-segment proposals to the observed allocation pattern and actual feature gates; do not combine incompatible controls or import comment thresholds as defaults.
Treat cache release as synchronization/allocation work at a quiescent boundary; compare identical allocation sequences in fresh processes at the same synchronization points.
